title: Design System: NET
scope: Suspended Field is the target system, applied today only to the landing page `/` via `.world-field` (web/src/app/world-field.css). /docs and /games still run the legacy root @theme in web/src/app/globals.css until a planned second pass; do not extend the legacy theme.

ink-faint-on-panel.note: Re-declared as --color-ink-faint inside the slab utility; --color-ink-dim is not overridden on panels.

display.purpose: Hero area title only; uppercase; exactly two lines.

headline.purpose: Every section title; uppercase, max 19em, balanced, at most two lines; each phrase pulled into focus on scroll.

lede.purpose: Opening paragraph of the hero and of a section, in astral ink.

body.purpose:
Running prose, 17px in astral ink, capped at 70ch. All

in the world default to Archivo.

numeral.purpose: Measured figures in stat panels, with a 10px mono unit beside them.

label.purpose: Section markers (vertical in the right margin at 1024px+, flat at the section foot below), panel IDs, document refs, footer meta.

data.purpose: Event tails, code, ASCII diagrams; smallest data steps are 12-13px.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Only panels that float: the axiom wave and the shared-rhythm panels. Panels at rest cast none.

shadows.name: attended
shadows.purpose: Panel lifted on hover/focus, with a 5px rise.

shadows.name: seam-glow
shadows.purpose: Spill under the seam of an attended panel.

shadows.name: held-seam-glow
shadows.purpose: Spill under the seam of a held panel.

shadows.name: blackwall-wordmark
shadows.purpose: Legibility of the BLACKWALL wordmark over its concrete pillars. That element only.

motion.name: ease-field
motion.purpose: The one easing for displacement and hold.

motion.name: attend
motion.value: translateY(-5px) 0.6s; border, face, ticks 0.35s; seam scaleX(0.3 -> 1) 0.7s
motion.purpose: Hover/focus lift: the field picks up what you attend to.

motion.name: altitude-rank
motion.value: static offsets above a shared floor hairline: 0 / 40px / 96px

motion.name: migration-rail
motion.value: 7px marker crosses the rail in 6s linear; phase i lights (border #7a9a2c, number #c4ff3d) for its sixth, delay = i x 1s
motion.purpose: Progress shown along a rail, not by height; flat panels on one baseline.

motion.name: scarcity-mesh
motion.value: scroll-linked growth from the four 1969 nodes to a flat lattice; pingwave rings every ~1.4s over 1.6s once full
motion.purpose: §01 argument: four hosts become a mesh with no centre. Reduced motion: one still of the full mesh.

motion.name: field-wave
motion.value: translateY(-9px) peaking at 18%, 7s, delay = index x 0.28s
motion.purpose: Nine axioms: one wave in reading order, like a pingwave.

motion.name: field-sync
motion.purpose: Panels that are one live system (hero telemetry, the NET topology panel).

motion.name: focus-pull
motion.value: armed: translateY(0.35em), opacity 0.55, blur(6px) -> none; 1.3s transform, 1.1s opacity/filter; 110ms per phrase
motion.purpose: Section titles pulled into focus on scroll; never invisible, sharp without script.

motion.name: picture-attend
motion.purpose: Application panel photos regain colour on hover (and on focus for the linked games card).

motion.name: scenery
motion.value: Mikoshi plinths (Monolith) sway +/- 7deg over 14s with a 14px bob; Blackwall pillars bob
motion.purpose: Concrete scenery only; it carries no data, so it is exempt from the float rule.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All float, wave, sync, focus pull, rise, lift and scenery loops drop to static.

components.name: Ghost Field Button

components.name: Field Link

components.name: Lifting Panel
components.description: The terminal panel held in the field: corner ticks, scanlines, hairline border. Attention lifts it 5px, dims the border green and lights the seam.

components.name: Section Title with Pillar Stencil
components.description: Uppercase headline on at most two lines; the section label sits vertical in the right margin at 1024px+, flat at the section foot below, never above the heading.
components.html:
§03 / protocol properties

Nine axioms. One runtime.

narrative.overview:
The mesh is a force field. The landing is a dark, raw-concrete brutalist hall, held up by nothing visible: concrete shards turn in one cold light shaft in the hero, Mikoshi's plinths and the Blackwall's pillars hang in it. Inside that hall the information sits on **terminal panels**: near-black phosphor glass with a hairline border, faint scanlines and green corner ticks, the project's cyberpunk HUD surface. Where the subject has a real world (the machines and places Net is meant to run in), it is shown with **real photographs** from open collections, held in the panels like evidence. Where the argument is a shape (1969's four hosts becoming a mesh with no centre), it is **drawn live** inside a terminal panel.

Float carries meaning. Panels sit flat and still on aligned grids by default; sequence is shown by a marker travelling a rail, not by height. A panel leaves the floor only when its height says something: altitude encodes speed (NET above real-time above best-effort), a travelling wave encodes propagation (the nine axioms, like a pingwave), a shared rhythm encodes one live system (the hero telemetry). Hovering a panel lifts it a few pixels and lights its seam: the field picks up what you attend to. Titles come into focus rather than appearing: each phrase is pulled from a soft blur into place, never hidden.

The world is cyber-led and keeps the project's terminal telemetry, mono data and acid green, and refuses the dark-neon dev-tool page where every card floats, glows and differs for no reason.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials: procedural cast concrete for scenery, terminal glass for every text-bearing panel and live diagram, real pictures for the subject's world.
Acid green carries one meaning: the field (live, held, attended, Net's side of a contrast, or the one primary action).
Monumental geometric caps (TeX Gyre Adventor, Avant Garde lineage) for titles; Archivo for prose; JetBrains Mono for data, code, telemetry, labels and controls.
Square corners, equal page margins, aligned equal grids; height above the floor is data, never ornament.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Field Green means the field: live, held, attended, Net's side of a contrast in the copy ("net assumes abundance.", "MOVES", "post-cloud."), or the one primary action. On a panel it appears only as the corner ticks (60% at rest, full when attended), the dim border when attended, and the seam. It is never a panel fill, a section background or a bright border at rest.

rules.name: The Panel Ink Rule
rules.body: Inside a panel, only the faint ink is raised (`ink-faint-on-panel`); dim and primary ink keep their ground values. Get it by putting text inside the `slab` utility, not by hand-picking a grey.

rules.name: The No Red Rule
rules.body: The palette has no red. Warnings are amber. Inherited terminal window dots are neutralised to grey and dim green inside the world.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Adventor for structure, Archivo for sentences, JetBrains Mono for anything a machine would print. Never set prose in mono, never set a number readout in Archivo.

rules.name: The Two Line Rule
rules.body: A section title runs on one or two lines, never a stack. The hero title is exactly two.

rules.name: The Focus Pull Rule
rules.body: A title is never invisible. Below the fold it waits slightly soft and low (0.35em down, 55% opacity, 6px blur) and is pulled into focus phrase by phrase as it enters view; without script it is simply sharp.

rules.name: The Meaningful Float Rule
rules.body: A panel leaves the floor only when its height encodes something: rank, propagation, shared state, or the visitor's attention. Sequence and progress travel along a rail instead. If you can't say what the height means, the panel rests. No random bobs, no per-card offsets, no idle drift on panels. All of it stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Shadow Follows Height Rule
rules.body: A panel on the floor casts no shadow. Shadow is the evidence of altitude, so it appears exactly where a panel floats and nowhere else; the primary button is flat.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: The field shows itself on a panel as a single 1px green line along its bottom edge: grown from 30% width when attended, or always lit when held. Held is reserved for the statement panel of a section.

rules.name: The Held Not Hung Rule
rules.body: Panels are never wired to each other, railed or framed together; a panel's relationship to the page is its grid position. The only lines that join things are field threads between mesh nodes (the hero canvas, the Mikoshi route), and they are green because they are the field.

rules.name: The Three Materials Rule
rules.body: Concrete is for scenery (canvas shards, Mikoshi plinths, Blackwall pillars). Terminal glass is for anything that carries words or numbers. Real pictures are for the subject's world (places, machines). Live diagrams are drawn on canvas inside a terminal panel. Never put text on concrete, never make scenery out of panels.

rules.name: The Witness Rule
rules.body: Sourced pictures show the world Net lives in, never Net itself. A sourced photo is never presented as Net's product, customer, deployment or team, and it never appears without its credit and licence. The only image of Net's own product is the Rose & Blade frame on the Multiplayer Games card, which is the project's own footage and links to /games.

dos: **Do** scope new landing-world work under `.world-field` and build every text-bearing container from the `slab` utility, so the terminal face, corner ticks and raised faint ink (`#7f8479`) come with it.
**Do** keep every band on the shared margins (24px / 48px at ≥1024px), prose at or under 70ch, and panels on aligned, equal grids.
**Do** give a panel altitude, and its shadow, only to encode rank, propagation, shared state or attention; show sequence with a marker on a rail.
**Do** show the subject's real world with sourced, licensed pictures, credit each one in `field-credits.json`, and give each an alt text that says what it is.
**Do** move on the field ease (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), and keep every float, wave, sync, focus pull and lift behind `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** label simulated telemetry as SIMULATED and mark real interface fragments with `data-ui`.

**Do** keep the brand's deliberate terminal vocabulary, even where generic taste rules advise against it: mono telemetry, tracked uppercase labels, hairline borders and outlined panels with corner ticks, scanline texture, the frozen 01–06 / P.0n / § labels and panel IDs that the copy already carries, and green accent phrases in titles.
donts: **Don't** extend the legacy root theme (Major Mono Display, Space Grotesk, CRT scanlines, `#3df0ff` cyan, `#ff5e3d` warn) on any new surface; it survives only until /docs and /games migrate.
**Don't** float, offset, stagger or shadow a panel for variety; a panel on the floor is flat.
**Don't** present a picture as Net's product, customer or deployment, caption it with invented claims, or ship one without its source and licence.
**Don't** stack a title over three or more lines, or hide a title entirely before it lifts.
**Don't** put text on concrete or build panels out of concrete.
**Don't** use Field Green as a panel fill, section background or bright resting border.
**Don't** invent new numbered labels or kickers; the § / 01–06 / P.0n markers are frozen copy, carried, not a pattern to extend.
**Don't** round corners, use red, redaction bars, or `<<text>>` Board-style treatments.
**Don't** set prose in mono or titles in Archivo.
